summary: Alois Müller worked in linguistics and related fields. He held positions at the Vienna University Library (~1867–1900), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and served as Direktor at Graz University Library in 1879.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Aloysius Pieris studied at institutions including London, Sri Lanka, Tilburg, and under Bernard de Give. In 1974, he founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre, later holding visiting chairs at WTU, UTS, and Vanderbilt.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1980 to 1985 under Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford (~1986–1988) and Harvard University (~1988–1995). He held faculty posts at UC Santa Cruz (~1996–2003), UC Berkeley (from ~2003), and the City University of New York (~2011–2012).

Indologist and religious studies scholar Alvappillai Veluppillai studied at the University of Peradeniya and Oxford under Thomas Burrow. He held posts at Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (2002–2009).

Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1936–1937). He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968), as an advisor for UNESCO (1968–1970), and as a Fellow at IIAS.
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under T. R. V. Murti and Michel Hulin.

Amanda K. Goodman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr. She holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Alasdair Urquhart, and Rahul Sankrityayan.

Amaranatha Jha worked in Indology and other fields, earning his B.A. at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at Jadavpur, Delhi, the London School of Economics (~1971–1977), and Harvard University (~1987).

Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Having studied under teachers including M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, and Susan Neiman, she has held posts at the University of York, Yale-NUS College, and as an Einstein Fellow in 2008.

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford by 2012. Her positions include Assistant Professor of IndoTibetan Buddhism at Naropa University and online faculty at Central Michigan University.

Amin Sweeney worked in linguistics and related fields, completing his doctorate at the University of London (~1967–1970). He taught at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (1970–1977) and chaired South and Southeast Asian Studies at UC Berkeley in 1998.
Amita Chatterjee is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian who earned her PhD at the EPHE under Ariane Macdonald. She has held posts at the CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She received her PhD from Columbia University (~2002–2008) and became assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2014.

Amy Sims Miller is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Virginia, completing her PhD in 2004 under David Germano, alongside studies with traditional Tibetan teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (1990, 1993) and held a post at the University of Washington around 1995.
